- Current constraints you mentioned: bursty traffic (hourly spikes during PR drops), strict SLA for search freshness, and on-prem requirement for PII workloads.
- Action items: 
  1) I'll send our latency/throughput benchmarks for the model variant we discussed.
  2) David will scope a short demo of our Dedicated routing and autoscale options to show steady-state throughput.
  3) You indicated procurement may want a short SOC2/architecture summary — happy to route that to your security contact.

Next steps I own: send the benchmark PDF + quickstart guide by EOD Friday. If you want a follow-up demo the week of Jun 15, suggest a 30-min slot (we can do 15 if you prefer).

If priorities have shifted since the call, let us know — otherwise I'll send the benchmarks as planned.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: ACME — latency/throughput benchmarks and notes (PDF attached)

Hi Alex / Priya,

Per our call, attaching the latency and throughput benchmark pack for the model we discussed. Highlights up front:

- Baseline (single-GPU, int8 quantized, RTX-class): median latency ~18ms, p95 ~48ms, p99 ~78ms for 512-token generation (sampling load, prompt+50 token output).
- With batching and KV caching (typical request locality): p95 drops to ~35ms at 8QPS sustained, throughput scales linearly with dedicated pools to 120 QPS per 8-GPU pool depending on sequence distribution.
- Fallbacks: we include a smaller ~4GB quantized variant that trades 10-15% quality for 2x lower p95 in constrained capacity scenarios.

Attached: acme_latency_benchmarks.pdf (detailed tables + plotting), redwood-quickstart-guide.pdf. Also linking the HubSpot deal and a Drive copy: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1A2b3C_acme_latency_benchmarks.

A few technical clarifications requested on the call:
- For the p99 numbers we observed some tail variance at very high concurrency; this is primarily driven by garbage collection pauses in the host process for our benchmark harness. In our real runtime, KV cache hit rates and continuous batching reduce observed tails.
- We can share live benchmarks under your workload if you'd like — that requires a quick tokenized prompt set and a short traffic replay.

Let me know if the numbers align with your expectations or if you want David to run a short demo next week to show autoscale and routing.

Thanks,
Marissa
[Attachment: acme_latency_benchmarks.pdf (pdf, 2.4MB)]
